items.answer: Extended reality (XR) is an umbrella term, not a specific technology, that covers all present or future immersive technologies, such as augmented reality (AR), virtual reality (VR), and mixed reality (MR).

Augmented reality (AR) is an enhanced version of reality created by technology, in which computer-generated digital content is overlaid on the real world in real time and registered in 3D, so the user perceives and interacts with the enhanced environment.
Mixed reality (MR) is an immersive technology that is the same as augmented reality, in which digital content is overlaid on the view of reality and can be interacted with.

Immersive technology is a technology that produces an experience in which a person perceives an environment through sensory organs as real, so that they cannot distinguish it from their real environment.

An immersive experience is a perceived experience through sensory organs that appears real, because a person cannot distinguish the experienced environment from their real environment and perceives it as that real environment.

questions.question: Why can a small share of XR applications in the military still be commercially important?
options: Because huge worldwide military budgets make a small percentage a large monetary amount
Because a smaller military budget makes a small percentage a large monetary amount
Because military applications use less hardware than video games, making them a large monetary amount
Because many military applications make a small percentage a large monetary amount
questions.explanation: The value comes from the size of military budgets, not from a large number of military applications or cheaper hardware. Even a small percentage of a huge budget can be a large amount of money.

questions.question: How can immersive simulations help medical education when obtaining cadavers is difficult?
options: They let learners study organs, their appearance, their parts, and how they work without a physical cadaver
They let learners replace MR-based diagnosis with VR displays in hospital operating rooms without a physical cadaver
They let learners avoid all practical training by reading organ diagrams without a physical cadaver
They let learners train on live patients before any organ study is completed without a physical cadaver
questions.explanation: Immersive simulations are useful in medical education because they allow learners to explore organs and their function when physical cadavers are unavailable. They are not a substitute for diagnosis, live-patient training, or reading diagrams.

questions.question: Why can VR help a buyer considering an upcoming property?
options: It lets them inspect a property after it is fully completed and make informed decisions before large spending
It lets them explore a property that may not yet exist and make informed decisions before large spending
It lets them sign a purchase contract immediately and make informed decisions before large spending
It lets them visit a property in person first and make informed decisions before large spending
questions.explanation: VR is useful in real estate because buyers can explore upcoming properties, even ones that do not yet exist, without visiting the place and before committing large amounts of money.

questions.question: How can digital heritage preservation help a heritage place that cannot be physically visited by many users?
options: It lets users explore each part virtually while preserving the space despite physical decay
It lets users close the site to all research while preserving the space despite physical decay
It lets users remove heritage objects from the site while preserving the space despite physical decay
It lets users enter the protected site physically while preserving the space despite physical decay
questions.explanation: Digital preservation is valuable because it lets people explore heritage places virtually even when physical access is limited, and it preserves the space digitally as it decays.

questions.question: What is an advantage of virtual tourism for someone who wants to visit a faraway place?
options: It lets users replace the place with a local recreation and saves money and physical effort
It lets users experience the place without physically going there and saves money and physical effort
It lets users travel to the place by video call and saves money and physical effort
It lets users visit the place after a full physical tour is completed and saves money and physical effort
questions.explanation: Virtual tourism and virtual tours allow users to visit faraway places without physical travel, saving money and physical effort. They do not require a video-call trip, a prior physical tour, or a local recreation.

data.text: XR’s commercial promise rests on forecasts of broad use, even though adoption statistics can be misleading and even a small military share can be large in value. Current VR use is organized by domain, from gaming and healthcare to education, automobile, travel, heritage, real estate, and defense. Each domain is connected to a practical immersive use, such as play, medical training, virtual tours, property exploration, or specialized defense training.
points: Although adoption statistics can mislead, XR forecasts show commercial potential, including a large-value military market.
The major current virtual reality application domains are gaming, healthcare, education, automobile, travel, real estate, and defense.
Gaming uses VR headsets for immersive play, while healthcare uses VR and MR for medical education and training.
Education, automobile, travel, and heritage are developing virtual reality areas for learning, car previews, tours, and preservation.
Real estate and defense are prominent virtual reality areas for exploring properties and for specialized defense training.

questions.question: Which sensory arrangement characterizes a non-immersive VR system?
options: unblocked access to real-world senses
partial blocking of real-world senses
virtual replacement of real-world senses
complete blocking of real-world senses
questions.explanation: A non-immersive VR system keeps the user's eyes, ears, and other sensory organs open to the real world. Semi-immersive systems block some real-world senses, while fully immersive systems block them completely.

questions.question: What determines a VR system's immersion category?
options: the number of devices worn by the user
the price paid by the user
the degree of sensory blocking
the industry sector chosen by the user
questions.explanation: VR systems are grouped as non-immersive, semi-immersive, or fully immersive according to how much real-world sensory input is left open. The number of devices, the price, or the application sector does not itself define the immersion category.

questions.question: Why are many commercial immersive VR applications semi-immersive?
options: they give physical presence while translating blinks into virtual actions
they give partial immersion while leaving some real-world senses exposed
they give full immersion while replacing the user's sense of reality
they give no immersion while keeping the user on a regular screen
questions.explanation: Semi-immersive VR is common in commercial immersive applications because it provides a partial immersive experience without blocking every real-world sense. Full immersion is costly and rare, while no immersion does not match commercial immersive applications.

questions.question: What makes a VR system fully immersive rather than semi-immersive?
options: it lets the user move through a virtual tour with a common headset
it replaces the user's sense of reality with virtual realism
it keeps the user physically attached to a real-world room
it leaves some real-world senses exposed while blocking vision
questions.explanation: A fully immersive VR system blocks the user's ability to sense the real world, so the user feels physically present in the virtual world. Leaving some senses exposed or using a common headset for a virtual tour describes semi-immersive VR, not fully immersive VR.

data.text: VR immersion is defined by the degree to which real-world sensory input is blocked. This sensory blocking produces three VR system categories: non-immersive systems engage attention without blocking senses, semi-immersive systems block only some senses and are the common commercial form, and fully immersive systems block all real-world senses with many tracking devices. The categories thus form a spectrum from ordinary computer engagement to complete virtual presence, with full immersion being the costliest and rarest.
points: VR immersion means the user's senses are blocked, so input comes only from the virtual world.
VR systems are categorized as non-immersive, semi-immersive, or fully immersive by how much real-world sensory input is blocked.
Non-immersive VR is a limited computer application that fully engages attention, while the user's senses remain open.
Semi-immersive VR blocks some but not all senses, often via a headset, and is common and cost-effective commercially.
Fully immersive VR blocks all real-world senses, tracks body movements via many devices, and is costly and commercially rare.

questions.question: Why are virtual reality headsets common in commercial immersive applications even though fully immersive systems provide stronger immersion?
questions.reference_answer: Virtual reality headsets are common in commercial immersive applications because most such applications are semi-immersive and cost-effective. A headset gives partial immersion by blocking some senses, such as sight, while ears and skin can still receive real-world signals. Fully immersive systems block all senses and are the costliest and commercially rare form.

questions.question: Why is World of Warcraft an example of a non-immersive virtual reality system even when a player is psychologically absorbed in the game?
questions.reference_answer: World of Warcraft is non-immersive because it is a specific gaming application that runs on a regular computer or console with ordinary displays and input devices. The player controls characters or activities while retaining control of the physical environment, and the virtual environment does not directly interact with the user. Although such software can take the user's attention, the user's sensory organs remain open and the user remains physically attached to the real world.

questions.question: How do virtual tourism and digital heritage preservation differ as immersive applications in travel and tourism?
questions.reference_answer: In travel and tourism, virtual tourism and digital heritage preservation serve different purposes. Virtual tourism lets users visit faraway places without physically going there. Digital heritage preservation targets heritage places that cannot be physically visited by large numbers of users or in all parts for preservation reasons; it lets users explore each part virtually, preserves the space digitally despite physical decay, and increases the space's lifespan and potential to be visited by more users.
